overview: Today's briefing covers key developments across global policy, commercial real estate markets, San Francisco local affairs, and Hawaii governance. In commercial real estate, new analyses examine whether policy adjustments can accelerate California's slow construction pace alongside major national property financings. San Francisco updates focus on municipal policy challenges, local elections, and housing development barriers. Meanwhile, Hawaii reports on key state government actions, including a Supreme Court order regarding the Elections Commission and discussions surrounding state correctional facilities.

items.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.summary: The United States has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine to help counter ballistic missile attacks.

items.title: Irvine Company Secures $157M Multifamily Refi in L.A.’s Playa Vista
items.summary: Irvine Company secured a $157.2 million refinancing loan from Capital One for a 309-unit luxury apartment property in Los Angeles' Playa Vista.

items.title: Is Prop 45 a Quick Fix to California’s Slow Construction Pace?
items.summary: Commercial real estate observers question whether Prop 45 can serve as a quick fix to California's notoriously slow construction and housing production pace.

items.title: Why nothing gets built in San Francisco
items.summary: San Francisco continues to grapple with high housing development costs that prevent new residential projects from penciling out.

items.title: ICE vehicles parking in San Francisco-owned garage, possible violation of sanctuary law
items.summary: SFMTA confirmed that ICE vehicles have been assigned parking spaces inside a city-owned garage, raising potential sanctuary law violations.

items.title: Supreme Court Orders Hawaiʻi Elections Commission Back To Work
items.summary: The Hawaii Supreme Court ordered the Elections Commission back to work, ending a five-month impasse just before the general election.

items.title: Plans For New Jail To Include Community-Based Treatment
items.summary: State officials advancing plans for a new jail intend to include community-based treatment alternatives to replace the overcrowded Oahu facility.

wiki.title: Zombie Nightmare
wiki.extract: Zombie Nightmare is a 1987 Canadian zombie film produced and directed by Jack Bravman, written by John Fasano, and starring Adam West, Jon Mikl Thor, Tia Carrere, Frank Dietz, and Linda Singer. The film centres on a baseball player who is killed by a group of teenagers and resurrected as a zombie by a voodoo priestess. The zombie goes on to kill the teenagers, whose deaths are investigated by the police. The film was shot in the suburbs of Montreal. It was originally written to star mostly black actors, but at the request of investors, the characters' names were changed to more typically white names. While Bravman was credited as director, Fasano directed the majority of the film; problems occurred between Fasano and the production crew, who believed him to be the assistant director and ignored his instructions.
